title: Base change of the global orientation
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$\Lambda=A$. For every morphism $v:Y'\to Y$, with $s'$ the zero
section of $\mathbf A^1_{Y'}$, the
exceptional
base-change comparison identifies $Lv^*\operatorname{pur}_s$ with the
orientation $\operatorname{pur}_{s'}$ for $\mathbf A^1_{Y'}$ of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation].

proof.text: Work with $Y,Y'$ in the fixed separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting, with the same finite coefficient ring $A$ and the affine-line datum [def-pur-affine-line-datum]. Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $X'=\mathbf A^1_{Y'}$, $g=\mathbf A^1_v$, $Z=s(Y)$, and $Z'=s'(Y')$. On affine charts $g$ sends $t$ to $t'$ and $R'[t']\otimes_{R[t]}R=R'[t']/(t')=R'$. Hence the square $(s,s',v,g)$ is Cartesian and its open complement is $(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\mathbf G_{m,Y'})$. In particular no flatness or reducedness of either base is needed. Set $K=A_Y$, $K'=A_{Y'}$, $F=A_X(1)[2]$, and $F'=A_{X'}(1)[2]$.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: write the Cartesian square and the coordinate pullback explicitly

proof.text: Write $S=Rs_!$, $R=Rs^!$, and $S'=Rs'_!$, $R'=Rs'^!$. The zero sections are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], so the identity-open compactifications in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] give $S=Rs_*$ and $S'=Rs'_*$. Use the class-restricted adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], with counit $\epsilon:SR\to\mathrm{id}$. By [lem-pur-gysin-structure], $RF$ is bounded constructible, in fact a lisse rank-one sheaf in degree zero. Thus $K$ and $RF$ have bounded etale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Pullback of a finite locally constant sheaf is finite locally constant: a covering which trivializes it pulls back to a covering with the same constant module. Exact finite-level pullback is [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so the primed adjunction also applies to $Lv^*RF$. Put $B=Lg^*$ and $V=Lv^*$. The compact-support exchange [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] gives $\beta_M:BSM\xrightarrow{\sim}S'VM$ for $M=K,RF$. Define the exceptional comparison $\chi_F:VRF\to R'BF$ as the mate of $\beta^{-1}$, namely the transpose of $B\epsilon_F\circ\beta_{RF}^{-1}$ under $S'\dashv R'$, as prescribed in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Exact inverse image preserves the constant sheaf, so $VK=K'$. For the twist, put $m=\ell^N$ as in the datum. [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies etale $g^{-1}\mu_m$ with $\mu_m$ on $X'$ and therefore identifies the tensor twists. The comparison-pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], together with the datum's specified comparison $\nu^{-1}(\mu_m^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes A)\cong A(1)$, gives $BA_X(1)=A_{X'}(1)$. On root sections the map is $u\otimes a\mapsto g^*u\otimes a$; its compatibility with the coefficient insertion follows by setting $a=1_A$. Exact pullback commutes with the shift, so $BF=F'$. This forms the comparison; no invertibility of $\chi_F$ is assumed.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: replace the inadmissible reference by the actual exceptional-adjunction mate

proof.text:
The complements of $s$ and $s′$ are quasi-compact open immersions: on every affine base chart they are the principal opens $D(t)$ and $D(t′)$. Thus [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] makes $s_*$ and $s′_*$ exact on the finite constant coefficient module sheaves, and identifies $S=Rs_*=s_*$ and $S′=Rs′_*=s′_*$ on the bounded-below categories. For a supported class represented under the natural identification [lem-pur-supported-hom] by $c:SK\to F$, its pullback to $(X',Z')$ is represented by $Bc\circ\beta_K^{-1}:S'K'\to F'$. This is the supported pullback: in the kernel-of-restriction definition [def-pur-support-cohomology], pullback takes a section vanishing on $X\setminus Z$ to one vanishing on $X'\setminus Z'$; the natural derived identification of [lem-pur-supported-hom] reads that map through the canonical closed-support source comparison $\beta_K$. Write $\alpha:K\to RF$ for the transpose of $c$, so $c=\epsilon_F\circ S\alpha$. The transpose of $\chi_F\circ V\alpha$ is, by the definition in step 2 and naturality of $\beta$,
$$
B\epsilon_F\circ\beta_{RF}^{-1}\circ S'V\alpha
 =B\epsilon_F\circ BS\alpha\circ\beta_K^{-1}
 =B(\epsilon_F\circ S\alpha)\circ\beta_K^{-1}
 =Bc\circ\beta_K^{-1}.
$$
Consequently the exceptional comparison on $V\alpha$ corresponds exactly to supported-cohomology pullback. The calculation uses only functorial composition and the natural adjunction bijection from step 2; it does not identify ordinary inverse image with $Rs^!$.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence and geometric-fibre sentence: identify the particular comparison on supported classes, including the transpose calculation

proof.text:
The class corresponding to $\operatorname{pur}_s$ is $\partial\kappa(t)$ by [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and [lem-pur-gysin-structure]. Clause (4) of [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer] gives $g_U^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t')$ on the punctured lines, with precisely the fixed finite-torsion pro-etale twist. Functoriality in the pair and coefficient sheaf in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] then gives
$$
g_Z^*(\partial\kappa(t))=\partial(g_U^*\kappa(t))=\partial\kappa(t').
$$
Here $g_Z^*$ denotes the map on supported cohomology of step 3. Thus step 3 associates to $\chi_F\circ V\operatorname{pur}_s$ the supported coordinate boundary on $X'$.

source.place: Proof, Kummer-class compatibility sentence: use geometric Kummer pullback and functoriality of the support boundary

proof.text: For a geometric point $q:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$, the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t']$, its origin is $V(t')$, and its punctured line is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t',t'^{-1}]$. The geometric-point clause of [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer] applies even if $\Omega$ is not finite over $k$: the coordinate class pulls back to $\kappa_A(t')$. Apply the pair functoriality of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] again to the class of step 4. Its supported restriction is $\partial\kappa_A(t')$, whose residue is exactly $1_A$ by [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation], also in the finite-torsion pro-etale formulation. Hence every geometric restriction of $\chi_F\circ V\operatorname{pur}_s$ is the normalized class $1_A$. This argument uses a single geometric point over $Y'$ and its composite with $v$, with the same algebraically closed field $\Omega$; it does not assert that $\Omega$ is the residue field of the image point.

source.place: Proof, geometric-fibre sentence: compute the actual coordinate residue rather than saying it transports

proof.text:
By [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation], $\operatorname{pur}_{s'}$ has those same normalized geometric restrictions. The injectivity in [prop-pur-affine-line-orientation-uniqueness], applied over $Y'$, therefore gives
$$
\chi_F\circ Lv^*(\operatorname{pur}_s)=\operatorname{pur}_{s'}
$$
after the constant-source and twist identifications in step 2. This is the asserted equality under the exceptional base-change comparison. For the empty base the Hom group is zero and the same injectivity gives the equality without choosing a geometric point.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: conclude by the prescribed global uniqueness
